title: GCD Stack
description:
Design a stack `GcdStack` of positive integers that supports standard LIFO operations alongside retrieving the **Greatest Common Divisor (GCD)** of all elements currently in the stack in `O(1)` time.

Implement the `GcdStack` class:
- `GcdStack()` initializes an empty stack.
- `void push(int val)` pushes positive integer `val` onto the top of the stack.
- `void pop()` removes the top element of the stack.
- `int top()` returns the top element of the stack.
- `int getGcd()` returns the GCD of all elements currently in the stack.
constraints: Methods pop, top, and getGcd are always called on non-empty stacks.
At most 3 * 10^4 calls will be made across all methods.
hints: Just like `min`, `gcd` is associative, so maintaining a parallel prefix-GCD stack lets every `pop`, `top`, and `getGcd` run in O(1).
On `push(val)`, push `val` onto the value stack and `gcd(val, gcdStack[-1])` (or `val` if empty) onto the GCD stack.

examples.explanation: gcd(12) = 12, gcd(12, 18) = 6, gcd(12, 18, 9) = 3; after popping 9, gcd(12, 18) returns to 6.
After pushing 7 and 14, gcd is 7; pushing 15 drops gcd to 1; popping 15 restores gcd to 7.
A single element 100 has gcd 100 and top 100.
